title: Mayliss Vane, Assayer Sovereign — Portrait
purpose: Mayliss is Edric's direct handler — the woman who commissioned the Seal of Unmaking job and expects it delivered. She is the gatekeeper to Count Marrow, the person who manages his affairs of acquisition, and the one who brokered the Triune's arrangement. The party has decided not to return the Seal to her, which makes her a looming complication: at some point Edric will have to face the woman he owes an artifact to and explain why she is not getting it. This portrait should establish her immediately as someone who has already assessed you, found the number, and is waiting to see if you match it. She is not Marrow's muscle and she is not his conscience — she is his ledger, and everything that crosses her desk gets weighed.
subject: A middle-aged woman of sharp, composed precision in practical but immaculately maintained clothing. She is not nobility. She is not clergy. She is not military. She is the person who makes all three of those things function — the administrator, the evaluator, the one who signs off. Everything about her communicates competence so thorough it has become a form of authority. She does not need a title of birth or a sword or a vestment to command a room. She has keys, ledgers, and the Count's ear, and that is more than enough.

critical_direction.not_a_femme_fatale: Mayliss is NOT a seductive schemer, a dangerous beauty, or a woman who uses feminine wiles as a weapon. She uses COMPETENCE as a weapon. She is attractive in the way that someone who maintains themselves with disciplined precision is attractive — not glamorous, not adorned, just impeccably correct. The portrait should never suggest she is performing for the viewer. She is working. You happen to be in the room.
critical_direction.not_a_villain: Like Severin and Dorn, Mayliss is not evil. She serves Marrow because that is her role, and she performs it with absolute proficiency. Whether she knows the full truth of what Marrow has been doing with the whiteglass artifacts is an open question. She may be complicit, she may be a tool, she may be something more complicated. The portrait should not answer this question — it should make the viewer realize they cannot tell, and that inability is itself unsettling.
critical_direction.the_assessment: Her defining quality, like Severin's, is assessment — but where Severin assesses your soul, Mayliss assesses your value. She looks at you and sees what you are worth, what you can deliver, what you will cost, and whether the margin is favorable. This is not dehumanizing — it is simply how she processes the world. Everything is an appraisal. The portrait should make the viewer feel precisely, efficiently evaluated. Not judged — that implies moral dimension. Evaluated. Weighed. Numbered.

character.physicality: Middle-aged. Not young, not old — the age where competence has fully matured and the body has settled into the shape that efficiency demands. A face that is handsome rather than beautiful — strong features, defined bone structure, the kind of face that photographs well because everything is in clear proportion. No softness, no excess. She maintains herself the way she maintains her records: precisely, practically, without waste. Her build is unremarkable — neither imposing nor slight. She does not need to be physically notable. Her presence is in her attention, not her stature.
character.clothing: Practical, immaculate, and of excellent quality — but not showy. She dresses like a senior professional, not like nobility. The fabrics are good but the cuts are functional. Dark tones — deep browns, ink blacks, muted copper-reds — that do not show ink stains or wax drips (the occupational hazards of her work). Everything fits precisely. Nothing is decorative for its own sake. The one piece of visible adornment is a small golden scale pin at her collar — her badge of office, the Assayer Sovereign's mark. It is subtle, understated, and tells anyone who knows what it means exactly how much authority she carries.
character.the_hands: Critically important. Her hands tell her story. Fingers stained faintly with ink — not heavily, not like a scribe who has just been writing, but the permanent faint discoloration of someone who handles ink and documents every day of their life. The staining is in the cuticles and the side of the writing hand, the places that never quite come clean. Her hands are otherwise well-maintained — clean nails, no roughness, the hands of someone who works with paper and metal, not soil or stone. One hand may be near or touching a document, ledger, seal press, or ring of keys.
character.the_keys: A ring of keys at her belt that NEVER jingles — she holds them still by habit, pressing them against her hip with her forearm or tucking them into a fold of fabric. This is an unconscious practiced gesture — she has been silencing her keys for so long it is muscle memory. The keys themselves are varied — different sizes, different metals, some old, some new. They open everything that matters in Crest Aurelion: archives, vaults, collection rooms, the Count's private chambers. The keys do not jingle because Mayliss does not announce her arrivals.
character.the_scale_pin: A small golden scale pin at her collar — two balanced pans, the symbol of the Assayer's office. It is the only piece of gold on her person, and it is small enough that you might miss it unless you knew to look. But its placement — centered at her throat, the first thing at eye level when she faces you — is deliberate. She wears her authority where you will see it exactly when she wants you to.
character.expression: Composed. Attentive. Waiting. Her default expression is not hostile or warm — it is the focused neutrality of someone who is listening carefully and processing everything. Eyes that weigh you before you have finished speaking. A mouth that is neither smiling nor frowning but is held in the precise position of someone who will respond when they are ready and not before. She lets silences stretch until you fill them — and in the portrait, that silence should be palpable. She is not waiting for you to speak. She is waiting for you to reveal yourself.
character.eyes: The focal point. Dark, sharp, attentive. They do not search for lies the way Severin's do — they search for VALUE. What are you worth? What can you deliver? What will you cost? How much of what you are saying is real and how much is markup? There is intelligence in these eyes, and patience, and the particular quality of someone who has sat across from hundreds of people trying to inflate their worth and has never once been fooled.

setting.location: Her office or workspace within Crest Aurelion — the place where Marrow's business of acquisition is actually conducted. This is not the Count's throne room or audience hall. This is the working room behind the public face: a desk, ledgers, shelved records, a wax seal press, writing implements, a balance scale for weighing metals. The room is organized with ferocious precision — everything has a place, everything is in its place. There is no clutter, no personal decoration, no warmth. The workspace IS her personality externalized.
key_props: A desk or work surface with one or more open ledgers — columns of figures, inventory entries, the administrative machinery of a county's acquisitions
A wax seal press — heavy, brass, well-used, with a stick of sealing wax nearby (warm red, resinous)
A small balance scale — functional, not decorative, for testing metal purity and coin weight. The tool of her trade made physical
Shelved records behind her — bound ledgers, scrolled documents, sealed pouches. The archive of everything that has passed through her hands
Writing implements — a quill or pen, an inkwell with iron gall ink (the brownish-black ink that stains fingers permanently)
setting.depth_of_focus: Mayliss is sharp. The workspace is present and readable — enough to establish 'this is where the real work of power happens' — but secondary to the character. The organized precision of the setting reinforces her personality without competing for attention.
setting.lighting_note: Image-specific direction: a subtle warm/cool temperature contrast on her face — warm workspace candle or oil-lamp glow on the ledgers and one side of her face, cool gray overcast daylight from a side window on the other. Keep it deliberately understated — working light, not the dramatic dual lighting used for Severin.

sensory_details_as_visual_cues.note: Drawn from her established sensory profile. The ones that can inform the rendering should.
sensory_details_as_visual_cues.ink_stains: The permanent faint ink discoloration on her fingers — iron gall ink, which is brownish-black and never fully washes out. This is the most important single detail after her expression. It marks her as someone who does the actual work, not someone who delegates it.
sensory_details_as_visual_cues.sealing_wax: The warm red-brown of sealing wax visible somewhere in the scene — a fresh seal on a document, a stick of wax on the desk, a wax impression still cooling. The snap of a wax seal being pressed is one of her signature sounds — the visual evidence of that sound should be present.
sensory_details_as_visual_cues.the_silence_she_creates: Mayliss lets silences stretch until you fill them. A voice that asks questions like she already knows the answers. The portrait should feel like a silence — a pause in which you are being waited out. The absence of any urgency or impatience in her expression is itself a tool.
sensory_details_as_visual_cues.metal_testing: A faint hint of something astringent — the chemicals used to test metal purity. This cannot be shown directly, but the balance scale and perhaps a small vial or testing stone on her desk can suggest the presence of assaying tools.

color_palette: burnished copper — her signature color, present in her clothing accents and the warm tones of the workspace
ledger cream — the aged paper of her records, the documents on her desk
sealing-wax red — warm, resinous, the one vivid accent color in an otherwise muted palette
ink black — her clothing, the iron gall ink, the darkest tones of the composition
deep leather brown — her clothing base, the desk surface, the bound ledger spines
small golden accent — the scale pin at her collar, the balance scale, the only gold in the image and it is functional, not decorative
warm candlelight amber — the workspace illumination
cool gray daylight — from the window, contrasting with the warm interior light
the brownish-black of iron gall ink stains on her fingertips
mood: The quiet authority of absolute competence. This is not a woman who raises her voice. She does not need to. She controls the flow of goods, contracts, certifications, and access in Marrow County. Every artifact Edric has ever retrieved passed through her hands. Every arrangement the Triune has with Marrow was brokered by her. She is the mechanism through which power operates, and she knows the value of everything that crosses her desk — including you. The portrait should make the viewer feel the particular discomfort of being in a negotiation with someone who knows exactly what their position is worth and will wait as long as necessary for you to realize you cannot bluff her. For Edric, this face represents an obligation he has not met and a conversation he is not ready to have.
composition: Medium shot — head to mid-torso or waist. She is seated or standing at her desk, oriented slightly toward the viewer but with her attention divided between the viewer and her work — perhaps one hand on a ledger, eyes on the viewer, as if you have just walked in and she is deciding whether you are worth setting down her pen for. The desk and its contents fill the lower portion of the frame, establishing her context. The scale pin at her collar should be small but visible. The ink stains on her fingers should be visible when the viewer looks closely. Her face occupies the upper third, eyes meeting the viewer's with patient, evaluative attention.
details: The golden scale pin at her collar — small, balanced, the Assayer Sovereign's mark of office
Ink-stained fingertips — the permanent brownish-black discoloration of iron gall ink in the cuticles and along the side of her writing hand
The ring of keys at her belt, held still against her body — varied sizes and metals, silenced by habit
An open ledger on the desk with visible columns and entries — the real machinery of county administration
A wax seal press and a stick of sealing wax — the tools of certification and authority
A small functional balance scale on the desk — for testing weight and purity, not for decoration
Clothing that is practical, dark-toned, and immaculately maintained — no decoration, no excess, excellent quality
The composed, patient expression — eyes that weigh you, a mouth that will speak when it is ready, the silence of someone who never fills conversational gaps
Organized shelved records behind her — the archive that contains every transaction she has overseen
The contrast between the warm workspace candlelight and the cool gray daylight from the window
art_direction: Channel the quiet authority of a Dutch Golden Age interior — Vermeer's light on a subject who could be a merchant or a magistrate. The tone is institutional competence: this is the person who makes the system actually work, and the portrait should honor that specific, unglamorous, deeply dangerous form of power. Pay particular attention to the workspace details (the ledger, the seal press, the scale, the ink) because these objects ARE her character the way Severin's vestments are his and Dorn's armor is his. A professional space where consequential decisions are made quietly.
aspect_ratio: 2:3 portrait — vertical composition for a character portrait, giving room for the desk and workspace below and the shelved records above while keeping her face as the focal point
do_not_include: Glamour, beauty, or seductive presentation — she is competent, not performing
Noble finery, jewelry, or ostentatious clothing — she is a professional, not an aristocrat. The scale pin is her only adornment
Weapons or any suggestion of physical threat — her power is administrative, not martial
Warmth, kindness, or maternal energy in her expression — she is not unkind, but her default is professional neutrality
Clutter, mess, or disorganization in the workspace — immaculate order is a character trait
Gold or wealth on display — the only gold is the small functional scale pin. She handles wealth; she does not display it
Dark scheming or villainous atmosphere — she may be complicit in Marrow's plans, but she reads as professional, not sinister
Youth — she has the settled, mature authority of someone who has been doing this work for decades
